subject: Looking for documentation on theme_bw() for boxplot

messages.author: 921ee9874398dd75
messages.subject: Looking for documentation on theme_bw() for boxplot
parts:
I used ggplot2 to prepare boxplots of my data6 or 8 months ago, and have generated good plots using theme_bw() that now need a few tweaks to polish for publication. When I did them the first time, I was able to use the preliminary version of the ggplot book, but now cannot locate documentation that I need to modify the line weight on the boxplot rectangles. I did find a suggestion to use current.grobTree()but it fails with Error: could not find function "current.grobTree".

When I use a construction like
p <- ggplot(df2,aes(x=Adhesive, y=FailStress_MPa))+geom_boxplot(size=1.5)
I can control the line weight, but of course theme_bw() applied over top of it changes the line weights.
I have also used the "+ opts(<option>) construction to modify the axis text and title, but can't find any equivalent documentation on the parts of the boxplot itself, except for outliers.

I imagine the documentation exists, can someone point me to it? Or suggest a way to manipulate the weight of the boxplots within the b&w theme?

Thank you
Jane

messages.author: 921ee9874398dd75
messages.subject: Re: Looking for documentation on theme_bw() for boxplot
parts:
baptiste_auguie is correct, and I made a dumb mistake. I am documenting my error here as a cautionary tale. In short, I forgot that persistent behavior requires assignment eg
# This works and maintains the box line weight
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg)) +geom_boxplot(size=1.5)+ theme_bw()
p
p + theme_gray()

#This does not because the changes were not assigned to q
q <- qplot(x=factor(cyl), y=mpg, data=mtcars,geom="boxplot", xlab="Xlabel",ylab="Ylabel")
q
q + geom_boxplot(size=1.5)
q + theme_bw()

Finding my error also taught me how to apply a different box line weight to a qplot, which was one of my original goals.

Thanks.
Jane
